params.title: The Fox and the Moonlit Lantern

params.text:
Once, beneath a velvet sky scattered with stars, a young fox named Fern lived at the edge of a whispering forest. Fern was curious about everything: the silver tracks in the snow, the sleepy owls in the pines, and especially the warm golden light that appeared each night beyond the hill.

One evening, Fern followed the glow and found a tiny lantern hanging from an old apple tree. It swayed in the breeze, though there was no one there to tend it. A note tied to its handle read, “For whoever is lost.”

Just then, Fern heard a small cry. A field mouse had wandered far from home and could not find the path through the tall grass. Fern lifted the lantern in his teeth and led the mouse along the moonlit trail. Together they crossed a brook, passed beneath the sleeping hawthorn, and reached a snug little burrow tucked beneath the roots of an oak.

The mouse’s family greeted them with hugs and crumbs of honey cake. Before Fern left, the mouse asked, “Who will guide you home?”

Fern looked up. The lantern’s light had grown softer, but the moon was shining brightly above the trees. “I think,” he said, “that when you help someone find their way, the path remembers how to lead you home.”

And so Fern followed the moonbeams back to his den, where his mother wrapped him in a warm blanket of moss. From that night onward, the little lantern glowed whenever someone needed help. Fern never knew who had hung it in the apple tree, but he always carried it carefully—and he always came home before the last star blinked goodnight.

The end.

params.title: The Fox Who Followed the Moonlight

params.text:
Once, at the edge of a quiet forest, there lived a little fox named Fern. Fern loved the nighttime best, when the trees whispered softly and the moon painted silver paths across the grass.

One evening, Fern noticed that the moonlight had made a shining trail leading deep into the woods. Curious but careful, Fern followed it past the sleepy ferns, over a mossy stone, and beneath the branches of an old oak.

At the end of the trail sat a tiny lost star, glowing faintly in a patch of clover. It had tumbled from the sky and was too tired to find its way home. Fern curled her warm tail around the star and stayed beside it until the night wind grew gentle.

Then Fern had an idea. She climbed the old oak and called to the moon, "Please help my little friend." The moon shone brighter, and a silver beam lifted the star high above the treetops.

Before it vanished into the sky, the star twinkled three times. From that night on, whenever Fern looked up, one star always seemed to shine a little brighter than the rest. Fern would curl beneath the oak, close her eyes, and dream beneath her friend's gentle light.

And in the quiet forest, all was well.

The end.
